about: A workflow every account can find and run: reverse engineer how a company, product or creator grew, from public evidence only, into dated moves set against its growth and ten plays crossed with the person's own goal. Paid lookups go through the person's treg connection (tools/treg), each priced before its first call, inside a budget the person sets, with a stop after every step. One workflow-recipe row in the shape of the shared recipe shelf (job, input_schema, ordered steps, each with do, submit and checks).

payload.label: Reverse engineer how something grows
payload.job: For any target the person names (a company, product, app or creator): read its site, stack, partners, launches and funding, when its traffic turned, what it ranks for and which AI answers name it, its ads, who talks about it, its own content ranked top quartile against bottom quartile on each channel, its links and loops, and what it is hiring for; set the dated moves against its growth; map its customer path; then cross the moves with the person's own goal into ten plays. Every finding is SEEN (a call result or a page shows it, with its link) or INFERRED (reasoned from what was seen), or not seen. Public evidence only: no account is made, no form is filled and nobody is contacted. Every paid endpoint is priced before its first call, the run stays inside the person's budget, and after every step the person says continue, skip or stop.
payload.produces: A dated growth teardown of the target with every finding labelled SEEN or INFERRED, its moves set against its traffic, and ten plays the person can run, each with a ready prompt; in content mode, the patterns that separate the target's best posts from its worst on each channel.

source.name: REA growth: turn a company's growth history into a playbook (treg)
source.note: Adopted: the steps and their order, full and content modes, the SEEN and INFERRED labels with 'not seen' for anything unseen, public evidence only, the price read before an endpoint's first call, free routes first, a $3 default budget, one alternative endpoint when one fails, every count computed by code and dated, and a short finding with the next check and its cost after each step, then continue, skip or stop. Not adopted: calling treg through its command line (the calls go through the Workshop rows in tools/treg, paid by the person's treg connection); reading YouTube channel videos through a paid endpoint (tool:keep-channels-latest-videos-and-captions reads them on the person's computer for free and keeps the captions, which tool:cite-principles-from-captions then reads); writing playbook.md, playbook.html and CSV files in a folder (each step's submitted output is the record of the run). Endpoint ids and prices are as the catalog listed them on 2026-10-30; the run reads them again before spending.

target.description: What to reverse engineer: its site address, or its name when the site is not known, for example https://example.com

goal.description: What the person wants to grow, in their own words: their product or channel and the result they want; the plays are crossed with it

mode.description: full runs every step; content reads only the target's handles and own content and ends with the content report

budget_usd.description: The most the whole run may spend from the person's treg balance, in US dollars (default 3)

country.description: The market to read search data for (default US)

account.description: Which of the person's treg connections pays

handles.description: The target's social handles or channel addresses, if the person already knows them; the site step finds them otherwise

buyer_questions.description: Questions a buyer asks an AI before choosing in the target's market; the search step writes three when none are given

models.description: The chat model tool:say-why-a-technique-works and tool:cross-techniques-with-a-goal use, as they take it ({ writing: { url, model } })

steps.title: Settle the target, the mode, the budget and the price of the plan
steps.do: Ask for anything missing before any paid call: the target (when only a name is given, find its site with tool:read-public-web-page or, if that cannot, tool:search-the-treg-catalog for a web search endpoint, priced first), the person's goal, the mode, the budget (default 3 US dollars) and the country (default US). Call tool:read-my-treg-team with { "account": <input account> } and keep its org_id; call tool:read-my-treg-balance with that team_id and keep the balance as the run's starting balance. If treg refuses the token, stop and tell the person to sign in to treg and hold a new token in their treg connection. Read every endpoint this recipe's steps name for the chosen mode with tool:read-a-treg-endpoint-and-its-price (free): its method, inputs, cost.usd, cost.unit, whether it bills per call or per success, and its cost note (some add a charge per returned row; some need the person's own provider key and are then unavailable). Add the prices up with code into an estimate per step and a total. Show the person the plan with each step's estimate, the total, the budget and the balance, and ask: continue, skip a step, or stop.

domain.description: The target's site host, or none

within_budget.description: The estimate fits the budget and the balance; otherwise the person narrows the plan before going on

steps.title: Map the site: its pages, pricing, sign-up and handles
steps.do: Read the target's home page, pricing page and sign-up page with tool:read-public-web-page (free). List the rest of its addresses with tool:call-a-treg-endpoint on treg.web.map (POST, body { "url": <target>, "limit": 100 }); read a page the free reader cannot read with treg.web.extract (POST, body { "url": <page> }). Pass max_cost_usd at the price read for that endpoint. Record its pages, its prices and plans as written, the steps of its sign-up as seen, and every social handle or channel it links to (add the input handles). In content mode do only the handles. Every finding is SEEN with its address, INFERRED with what it is reasoned from, or NOT SEEN. Read tool:read-my-treg-balance and record what the run has spent. Tell the person the step's finding in three lines, what the next step checks and its estimated cost, and ask: continue, skip or stop.

checks.says: At least the home page was read
Every endpoint called was priced first

steps.title: Its stack, partners, launches and funding
steps.do: Skip in content mode. With the domain from the setup step call tool:call-a-treg-endpoint on predictleads.companies.technology_detections, predictleads.companies.connections, predictleads.companies.news_events and predictleads.companies.financing_events (each GET, the domain in query as its catalog entry names it), each at its price. Record the analytics, ads, payments and growth tools it runs with the date each was first seen, its partners and integrations, and each dated launch, hire, partnership and funding event. When an endpoint fails, find the same job with tool:search-the-treg-catalog, price and try one alternative, else record it as unavailable. Label every finding SEEN, INFERRED or NOT SEEN; dates as the source gives them. Read the balance, record the spend, and ask: continue, skip or stop.

checks.says: Every endpoint called was priced first

steps.title: When it grew: monthly search traffic and the turn
steps.do: Skip in content mode. Call tool:call-a-treg-endpoint on dataforseo.x.dataforseo-labs-google-historical-rank-overview-live (POST, body with the target domain, the location code and language for the input country, for example 2840 and en for the US) at its price, for the last 24 months. akta.x.website-traffic needs the person's own provider key: use it only when the catalog says their team holds one. Compute with code each month's estimated traffic and keyword count, the month-over-month change, and the month or months where growth turned (the largest sustained change in slope); date every count. Label every finding. Read the balance, record the spend, and ask: continue, skip or stop.

checks.says: Every endpoint called was priced first

steps.title: What it ranks for, and which AI answers name it
steps.do: Skip in content mode. Call tool:call-a-treg-endpoint on dataforseo.google.domain.ranked_keywords (POST, body with the target domain, the location and language for the input country, and a limit) at its price; its cost note adds a charge per returned keyword, so choose the limit with the person (1,000 keywords cost about ten times the floor). Group the keywords by intent with code: brand, comparison and alternative, problem, and job to be done; list the pages that earn the most estimated traffic. Then ask three buyer questions (the input buyer_questions, or three written from what the site sells) through cloro.ai-search.chatgpt.scrape (POST, one call per question) at its price, and record which brands each answer names and cites, in order, and whether the target is among them. Label every finding. Read the balance, record the spend, and ask: continue, skip or stop.

checks.says: Every endpoint called was priced first

steps.title: Its ads on Meta, Google, LinkedIn and TikTok
steps.do: Skip in content mode. With the brand name and domain call tool:call-a-treg-endpoint on scrapecreators.x.v1-facebook-adlibrary-search-companies then scrapecreators.x.v1-facebook-adlibrary-company-ads for the page it finds, serpapi.google.ads.transparency, adyntel.linkedin.search.ads.company and anyapi.tiktok.ad_library_search, each with the method and fields its catalog entry names, each at its price. Record per platform how many ads are running, the oldest still running (an ad that has run for months is one that pays), the offers, hooks and calls to action they repeat, and where they send people. Label every finding. Read the balance, record the spend, and ask: continue, skip or stop.

checks.says: Every endpoint called was priced first

steps.title: Who talks about it: founders, creators, users and press
steps.do: Skip in content mode. Call tool:call-a-treg-endpoint on anyapi.x.search.posts with a query of the brand name, a minimum like count (for example min_faves:300) and the founder's own posts left out (-from:<founder handle> when the site step found one), anyapi.youtube.search for the brand name, and scrapecreators.reddit.search.posts for the brand name, each at its price. Record who spread it (founder, creator, user, press), when, how far each post went, and the first post that went far. Label every finding. Read the balance, record the spend, and ask: continue, skip or stop.

checks.says: Every endpoint called was priced first

steps.title: Its own content, best quartile against worst, on each channel
steps.do: For each handle from the site step read the channel's recent posts. YouTube: tool:keep-channels-latest-videos-and-captions on the person's computer (free; it keeps each video's captions), then tool:cite-principles-from-captions over those captions for the principles the videos state or show, each with its quote and second. Other channels through tool:call-a-treg-endpoint, each at its price: scrapecreators.instagram.user.posts, crawl4ai.tiktok.user.videos, anyapi.x.user.posts.timeline (and tikhub.x.twitter-web-fetch-user-media for its pictures and videos), harvestapi.linkedin.company.posts. With code, rank each channel's posts by engagement for their reach (views, or likes, comments and shares when views are absent), date the counts, and split the top quarter from the bottom quarter. Compare the two quarters on title or first line (length, numbers or money, first person, a question, brackets, the promise), thumbnail or cover (face, words on it, contrast), hook, format and length, by looking at each image. Record each pattern with how many posts in each quarter show it. Label every finding. Read the balance, record the spend, and ask: continue, skip or stop.

checks.says: Only the target's own handles are read
Every endpoint called was priced first

steps.title: Its links and its loops
steps.do: Skip in content mode. Call tool:call-a-treg-endpoint on dataforseo.web.backlinks.summary and dataforseo.web.anchors.list (POST, body with the target domain and include_subdomains true) at their prices; each adds a charge per returned row, so keep the row limit the person agreed to. Record the referring domains and how they grew, the anchors that repeat, and every loop the product runs: a 'made with' or 'powered by' badge, shared links, templates, embeds, invites or referral pages, each with a page that shows it. Label every finding. Read the balance, record the spend, and ask: continue, skip or stop.

checks.says: Every endpoint called was priced first

steps.title: What it is hiring for next
steps.do: Skip in content mode. Call tool:call-a-treg-endpoint on predictleads.companies.job_openings (GET, the domain in query) at its price. Keep the roles first seen in the last 30 days, group them with code by function (growth, content, sales, partnerships, product, engineering), and say which channels the roles show it is about to scale. Label every finding. Read the balance, record the spend, and ask: continue, skip or stop.

checks.says: Every endpoint called was priced first

steps.title: Set the dated moves against its growth
steps.do: Skip in content mode. No paid calls. Gather every dated move the earlier steps saw (launches, funding, partners, the first post that went far, ads that started, loops, pages that began to rank, hires) and give each an id. With code, join them to the months of the when-it-grew step: for each move, the traffic in the three months before and after it, and whether a turn falls within two months after. A move that comes before a turn is a candidate cause, labelled INFERRED; nothing is called a cause because of timing alone. Show the person the table and ask: continue, skip or stop.

steps.title: Map its customer path
steps.do: Skip in content mode. No paid calls. From what the earlier steps saw, write the target's path in five stages: notice (where people first meet it), sign up, first win (the first result a new user gets and how fast), pay (what makes them pay and when), share (what makes them bring others). For each stage say what the target does, the page or post that shows it, and its label. Ask: continue, skip or stop.

steps.title: Cross the moves with the person's goal into ten plays
steps.do: Skip in content mode. No paid calls. Describe each move from the moves-vs-growth step as a technique with tool:say-why-a-technique-works (its mechanism and what it operates on), using the input models. Then call tool:cross-techniques-with-a-goal with the input goal, those rows, the vocabulary it returned and the input models, to find which moves serve the goal, which pairs compound, and which the person's situation rules out. Write ten plays, highest expected effect for the least effort first: each names the moves it rests on by id, what to do, why it worked for the target, how it fits the person's goal, and a ready prompt the person can give their AI to start it. Then the moves to skip and why, a timeline of the target's moves, and a 14-day plan. Show the person the plays and ask: done, or change.

checks.says: Every play rests on a move seen in this run

steps.title: The content report
steps.do: Only in content mode; skip in full mode. No paid calls. From the own-content step write, per channel: the patterns that separate the top quarter from the bottom quarter with their counts, the title and cover formulas they add up to (as slots the person fills), the principles the videos state with their quotes, and the top posts to study first. Show the person and ask: done, or change.

checks.says: Every top post named was ranked in the top quarter
